sections.h2: Routes to a closing in Bernards Township
sections.html:
You can list the house, sell it to a buyer you find privately, or accept a cash bid for the property as it stands. The township adds its own pre-sale steps to the state rules, so your pace depends on how quickly permits and inspections get cleared.

With median home values around $814,800, many buyers finance, and a listing draws them. A cash bid answers different problems: an inherited house in Basking Ridge, a property whose permits were never closed, a rental after the tenant leaves, or a seller who needs a closing date that will hold.

  • Agent listing: the highest potential price, a longer timeline and repair talks after the inspection.
  • Private sale: no agent fee, with pricing, marketing and township paperwork on your desk.
  • Cash buyer: condition does not stall the sale, and the bid is reduced for the work required.

Bernards Township has 28,594 residents, and owners live in 83.1 percent of the housing units. Median household income is $194,107 and median rent is $2,476. Home values sit far above the national median of $332,700. At these price levels buyers expect a clean permit file, and the township checks for one before any residential sale anyway.

Because buyers here often borrow large amounts, lenders look hard at the file. Gather your deed, your recent tax and sewer bills, permit records for any addition or finished basement, and the fire safety certification in one folder before the first showing. A seller who hands over complete records early tends to keep a contract on schedule.

sections.h2: What a seller must obtain before closing
sections.html:
Two things, both issued from 277 South Maple Avenue in Basking Ridge. The first is an inspection and certification of smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and a fire extinguisher from the Bureau of Fire Prevention. The second is a Construction Records Clearance from the Code Enforcement Division. Create a free account on the township's online portal to apply.

The township code requires a Construction Records Clearance before the sale of any residential structure, and both owner and purchaser can be held responsible if one is not issued. The inspector checks records for open construction or zoning permits, and any open permit must have its final inspection before the clearance issues. File at least 10 business days before the change of ownership. A violation carries a fine up to $1,000, up to 90 days in jail or up to 90 days of community service.

Construction Records Clearance fees

  • Create the free account on the online portal and file both applications.
  • Close any open construction or zoning permit before the records inspection.
  • Schedule the fire safety inspection for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and the extinguisher.
  • Send the clearance fee with the application, using the tier that matches your closing date.

The code exempts several transfers when no one changes occupancy, including title corrections, a transfer between spouses and a transfer by or to an executor or administrator distributing an estate. Mortgage refinancing and home equity loans are exempt as well.

If the inspector lists open permits, contact the permit holder or the contractor first. A final inspection can take time to book, and the clearance fee rises as your closing date nears, so a late fix costs real money. If you cannot finish the work, tell the buyer's attorney early and ask whether the clearance can be handled through the contract.

The Tax Collector posts a 2026 total rate of $1.661. Of that, $0.275 funds the county, $0.030 county open space, $1.077 the school district, $0.246 the municipality and $0.033 the library. Four installments fall on the first of February, May, August and November, and the 10th of each of those months is the last day of grace. Postmarks do not count; the payment must be physically in the office.

Sewer bills follow their own cycle, due January 1 and July 1 with a 30-day grace period. A closing in the middle of a quarter is prorated, so get a current balance on both the tax and sewer accounts from the Tax Collector.

Senior and veteran deductions exist. Seniors qualify at 65 or older on October 1 of the prior year, if they live in the home and stay under the income limit. Tell your attorney if a deduction is in place.

sections.h2: Do floods affect a Bernards sale?
sections.html:
They can. The Passaic River runs along the township's edge, and the township keeps a flood information page with flood zone maps for buildings, floodways, open space and township property. It also links to FEMA maps and elevation guides.

Ask a buyer's lender whether the property needs flood insurance, and look up the parcel on the township and FEMA maps before you list. A seller who can show an elevation certificate or a clear zone designation answers a common buyer question in the first week.

Interstate 78, Interstate 287 and U.S. Route 202 serve the township. NJ Transit's Gladstone Branch stops at Basking Ridge and Lyons stations on the way to Hoboken Terminal, and Lakeland Bus Lines runs a Route 78 rush-hour service from Bedminster to the Port Authority Bus Terminal.

The Bernards Township School District runs six schools, ending with William Annin Middle School and Ridge High School. Private options include Pingry School's upper campus in Basking Ridge and Saint James School. Name the commuter stations and schools in your listing so buyers see them early.

sections.h2: What changes when the buyer pays cash?
sections.html:
Paying cash takes out the lender's appraisal and most repair haggling. The Construction Records Clearance, the Bureau of Fire Prevention certification and the state transfer fee all stay in place. Agree up front who files each application, because the clearance fee climbs as closing nears.

Weigh offers by what you keep. A listing may fetch more, but commission, staging, inspection credits and holding costs come out of it. Above $1,000,000 the buyer owes an extra 1 percent fee beyond the seller's own transfer fee.

A workable order of steps: sign the contract, open the portal account the same day, book the fire safety inspection, file the clearance request, and ask the Tax Collector for balances. Your attorney then schedules the closing, the deed is recorded and you hand over the keys.

faqs.q: Is a smoke detector certificate the only thing Bernards Township asks for?
faqs.a: No. The Code Enforcement Division also issues a Construction Records Clearance before a residential sale. Its review looks for open construction or zoning permits, which need final inspections before the clearance is released.

faqs.q: How much does a Construction Records Clearance cost in Bernards Township?
faqs.a: It costs $40 if the request reaches the township more than 10 calendar days ahead of closing, $75 inside 10 days and $125 inside 4 days. File the application at least 10 business days before ownership changes.

faqs.q: When are Bernards Township property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, with grace through the 10th. The money must be in the Tax Collector's hands by then, since a postmark proves nothing. Sewer bills are due January 1 and July 1.

faqs.q: Which transfers skip the Bernards clearance?
faqs.a: A transfer is exempt when occupancy stays the same. That covers a deed correction, a transfer between spouses, an estate distribution by an executor or administrator, and refinancing or home equity loans.

faqs.q: Does the buyer ever pay a transfer fee in New Jersey?
faqs.a: Only when the price is above $1,000,000. The seller pays the standard realty transfer fee in every sale, and the buyer owes an added 1 percent above that line.
